ambiguities.description: The term 'Client' used by the billing system may or may not refer to the exact same concept/population as 'Customer' in the CRM. The Product Manager states they are 'the same concept' for modeling purposes, but also notes the billing team applies a stricter definition (only someone who has actually paid is a client), suggesting Client could be a subtype of Customer or a differently-scoped population rather than a true synonym. This is a deliberate terminology nuance raised in the final exchange of the transcript and is not fully resolved.

source_references.excerpt: I've heard some people call customers "clients" in the billing system. Are those the same thing?

In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether the uniqueness of an Order Line (Order + Product combination) is truly the identifying uniqueness constraint, or whether an order could have multiple lines for the same product (e.g., added at different times) each with its own quantity. The transcript only states that each line specifies a product and quantity, without clarifying whether duplicate products across separate lines are allowed.

source_references.excerpt: Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity.

ambiguities.description: The transcript does not specify whether a Product must appear in at least one Order (mandatory role for Product in the order line fact type), only that 'a product can appear in many different orders,' which describes a maximum/frequency aspect but leaves the minimum (mandatory participation) unstated.
